text: If Earth suddenly stopped spinning, even for one second, everything not bolted down would keep flying east at about a thousand miles an hour.
That's because right now, at the equator, you're already moving that fast. You just can't feel it, because everything around you moves with you.
So when the ground stops, you don't. Neither do cars, trees, houses, or even the air.
The atmosphere would keep racing along at supersonic speed, creating winds stronger than any tornado, scraping across the whole planet.
The oceans would keep moving too, sending giant walls of water miles inland.
And if Earth stayed stopped, things get even weirder. One day would last a whole year: about six months of sunlight, then six months of darkness.
Without the spin, the oceans would slowly flow toward the poles, and a giant new continent would rise around the middle of the planet.
But here's the crazy part. Earth actually is slowing down, right now.
When dinosaurs were alive, a day was about half an hour shorter. The Moon's pull is gently putting on the brakes.
Don't worry though. Each century, our day only gets about two thousandths of a second longer. So hold on tight... we're still spinning.
